paragraphs.text: Taking the opportunity of his adversaries words he describes the state of man's life from his birth to his death.
paragraphs.label: a
paragraphs.anchor: that is born of a woman

paragraphs.text: His meaning is, that seeing that man is so frail a creature, God should not handle him so extremely, in which Job shows the wickedness of the flesh, when it is not subject to the Spirit.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Until the time you have appointed him to die, which he desires as the hireling waits for the end of his labour to receive his wages.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: He speaks here not as though he had no hope of immortality but as a man in extreme pain, when reason is overcome by afflictions and torments.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: By this he declares that the fear of God's judgment was the reason why he desired to die.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: That is, relieve my pain and take me to mercy.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Meaning, to the day of the resurrection when he would be changed and renewed.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Though I am afflicted in this life, yet in the resurrection I will feel your mercies and answer when you call me.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: You lay them all together and do not allow any of my sins to go unpunished.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: He murmurs through the impatiency of the flesh against God, as though he used great severity against him as against the hard rocks, or waters that overflow, so that by this the opportunity of his hope is taken away.
paragraphs.label: k
paragraphs.anchor: rock is removed out of his

paragraphs.text: Yet while he is in pain and misery.
